as_written_in_papers.quote: A novel frameshift mutation referred to hemizygous mutation (c.1052delG) in exon 8 of LAMP2

cases.statement: Two people in two unrelated reports from different Chinese centres: a female (Family F7 III-8, PMID 33680117, written c.1054delG) and a hemizygous male proband (III-1, PMID 33933120, written c.1052delG). The pipeline normalised both strings to the same deletion.

people.label: Family F7 III-8
people.key_phenotypes: diagnosed at 23 years; fatigue, chest tightness, breathlessness; NYHA class III; LVEF 20.6%; premature ventricular contractions; MLVWT 8 mm

people.label: III-1
people.key_phenotypes: heart failure at 18 with LV hypertrophy, dilatation of all four chambers and LVEF 24%; WPW syndrome; mental retardation with learning difficulties since kindergarten; proximal limb and back muscle atrophy with CK 732 U/L; high myopia; vacuolar myopathy with glycogen on muscle biopsy; died after readmission for cardiogenic shock

quotes.quote: The proband (III-1), a male patient in early adolescence admitted to hospital on December 23, 2015 with heart failure (Fig. 1).
A novel frameshift mutation referred to hemizygous mutation (c.1052delG) in exon 8 of LAMP2 (Fig. 5) was revealed which predicted to cause truncation of the protein.
ECG showed sinus rhythm, atrial premature beat, WPW syndrome (Fig. 2).
Transthoracic echocardiography revealed left ventricular hypertrophy with dilatation of all four chambers, and diffuse decrease of wall movement
He also exhibited some mental retardation, learning and expressing difficulties, all of which were present in his kindergarten.
On the day of admission: physical examination revealed muscle atrophy of the proximal limbs and back.
He had a history of visual impairment and was diagnosed with highly myopic in elementary school, which was partially corrected with glasses.
Unfortunately, his family forewent invasive treatment and the proband died within 24 h of his second admission.

phenotype_specificity.statement: III-1 (PMID 33933120): the authors suspected Danon disease clinically and confirmed it with a muscle biopsy showing glycogen-filled vacuoles before sequencing; the paper does not say which genes besides LAMP2 were tested or whether they were negative. F7 III-8 (PMID 33680117): cohort-level panel statement only; her MLVWT of 8 mm sits outside the range the paper gives for the cohort.

quotes.quote: In combination with the symptoms, physical examination, laboratory tests, and medical history of the proband, we suspected DD as the underlying cause.
An unusual periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) staining was localized in the vacuoles, suggesting glycogen deposition (Fig. 4d).
The proband had all of the above-mentioned clinical triad associated with DD, as well as cognitive and neurological deficits

An exon and boarding intron analysis of 96 cardio disease-associated genes (Table SI) was performed in 770 patients with HCM using second-generation sequencing (11) at the HCM clinic in the Department of Ultrasound, Xijing Hospital (Xi'an, China) between May 2012 and February 2020.
All patients had an HCM phenotype on presentation with a mean MLVWT of 17 mm (range, 14-24 mm; Table I).

segregation.statement: PMID 33933120: three relatives tested (father, uncle II-3, cousin III-2) did not carry the variant and had normal ECG and echocardiography. The mother (II-2, heart disease at 24, sudden death 2 years later) and maternal grandmother (I-2, died of heart disease at 30) were not reported as tested. PMID 33680117: not reported for F7 (cohort-level summary only).

quotes.quote: The same mutation was not found in his father, uncle (II-3) and cousin (III-2) whose electrocardiogram and echocardiography are normal.
In terms of family genetic history, his mother (II-2) was diagnosed with ‘heart disease’ at the age of 24 and died suddenly 2 years later.
His maternal grandmother (I-2) died of ‘heart disease’ at the age of 30.

Regarding their occurrence in the pedigrees, four mutations were detected in one of their parents, one mutation was a de novo mutation and two mutations were not confirmed in their pedigree because their parents were not available.

de_novo.statement: Not shown in either paper. PMID 33933120: only the father was tested (negative); the mother was deceased and not tested. PMID 33680117: cohort-level summary does not identify the de novo family.

quotes.quote: The same mutation was not found in his father, uncle (II-3) and cousin (III-2) whose electrocardiogram and echocardiography are normal.

Regarding their occurrence in the pedigrees, four mutations were detected in one of their parents, one mutation was a de novo mutation and two mutations were not confirmed in their pedigree because their parents were not available.

functional.statement: PMID 33933120, patient muscle (vastus lateralis biopsy): immunohistochemistry with an anti-LAMP2 antibody showed LAMP2 expression in only a few intracytoplasmic vacuoles; no control tissue is described. PMID 33680117: none.

quotes.quote: Immunohistochemical analyses using a commercial anti-human LAMP2 antibody demonstrated only a few intracytoplasmic vacuoles displaying the expression of LAMP2 protein (Fig. 4e).

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Single-nucleotide deletion causing a frameshift (predicted p.(Val352PhefsTer6)) in exon 8 per PMID 33933120. Papers state loss of function as the disease mechanism and predict truncation.

quotes.quote: We describe here a novel exonic mutation in the LAMP2 gene (c.1052delG) that results in coding shift and may lead to premature truncation of the mutant LAMP2 protein.
It is caused by a loss-of-function mutation in the lysosome-associated membrane protein-2 (LAMP2) gene.

population_data_in_papers.statement: The methods say each variant was Sanger-sequenced in 300 healthy unrelated individuals; no per-variant result is given.

quotes.quote: The identified mutation was further confirmed by bidirectional Sanger sequencing among the remaining family members and 300 healthy unrelated individuals with normal ECG and echocardiographic findings and without any family history of cardiovascular disease.

authors_classification.statement: PMID 33680117 calls all seven LAMP2 variants disease-causing in its abstract and says five were new; PMID 33933120 calls c.1052delG novel and causal. Authors' words quoted.

quotes.quote: A pathogenic mutation in LAMP2 was identified in 7 patients who phenotypically presented with HCM.

Among the mutations, five were novel mutations, one mutation (c.928G>A) had previously been reported (17) and one mutation had been reported as a pathogenic mutation previously ClinVar (Aug 09, 2013; https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/clinvar/variation/179062/) but had not been reported in individuals or large population studies.

These findings suggest that this genetic mutation is actually pathogenic and that the novel mutation of exon 8 of LAMP2 may be relevant in determining phenotype severity, earlier onset of heart failure, certain risk of sudden death, worse prognosis, and severe cognitive and neurological impairment.

concerns: Numbering: PMID 33680117 writes c.1054delG and PMID 33933120 writes c.1052delG; the pipeline normalised both to NM_002294.3:c.1054del. This merge holds only if the deleted G lies in a run of Gs spanning c.1052-c.1054; the panel should confirm against the reference sequence. Neither paper states a transcript.

Protein: PMID 33680117 writes p.V352Ffs^*5; the protein predicted from the cDNA is p.(Val352PhefsTer6) (the batch protein_check says 'agrees', but the stop position differs by one). PMID 33933120 gives no protein change.
F7 III-8 and III-1 are different people (female aged 23 vs male proband aged 18 who died; different centres, Xi'an and Nanjing).
PMID 33680117 contradicts itself: Table I gives F7 III-8 an MLVWT of 8 mm, while the text says all seven had HCM with MLVWT 14-24 mm.
PMID 33933120 contradicts itself on age ('early adolescence' vs '18 years old') and refers to the male proband's 'her father'.

PMID 33680117 reports the family segregation only in Figure 1 (an image not in the text) and summarises it across the seven families without saying which family had which result, so parental status cannot be assigned to this person from the text.
PMID 33680117 says one of its seven variants had an earlier database entry and five were new, but does not say which variant is which apart from c.928G>A.
PMID 33680117 states 300 healthy controls were sequenced, but gives no per-variant result for them.
notes_for_panel: Two independent reports. The male case (PMID 33933120) has the fuller description, a muscle biopsy, and three relatives (father, uncle II-3, cousin III-2) tested negative; the paper does not say which side of the family the uncle and cousin are on. The mother, who had early cardiac death, was not tested. The female case (PMID 33680117) has only a table column.
